summary.headline: Latent View Q1 FY27 revenue fell 3.5% QoQ to USD 30.3M (INR 287 Cr, +21.6% YoY); FY27 growth guidance held at 12%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR 287 crore, up about 21.6% YoY but down 0.6% QoQ in rupee terms; dollar revenue fell about 3.5% QoQ to USD 30.3M, worse than the 1.5-2% decline guided. The drop was driven by CPG (Decision Point one-off projects not extended), a tech account insourcing (about INR 0.5 crore impact this quarter), and a one-time volume discount to a BFSI client (about USD 0.4M). Adjusted EBITDA was INR 58.6 crore (20.4% margin) after wage hikes for about 70% of staff (about 2.7 margin points). Management retained 12% FY27 growth guidance and 20-21% margin guidance, and expects a QoQ bounce-back from Q2. A new CEO, Sonal Ramrakhiani, joined only days before the call.

financial_highlights.change: Average hike about 8%, for ~70% of workforce
vs about USD 7.5M last quarter; FY26 about USD 5M net new, USD 17.5-18M consumption-linked

segments.name: Financial services (BFSI)
segments.commentary: Described as very strong execution this quarter, offsetting CPG softness; a large client grew to a run rate of about USD 10M annually, with a one-time volume discount granted.

segments.name: TMT / Technology
segments.commentary: Grew about 4% QoQ, but one large account was affected by consolidation and insourcing that cost about USD 7-8M of annual business; management expects part of the gap to be plugged in-year.

segments.name: Consumer goods (CPG, Decision Point)
segments.commentary: Key drag this quarter after Q4 one-off projects were not extended; management expects QoQ growth of 25%+ in Q2 and has about USD 2M of extensions and about USD 26M of pipeline. Added one new logo.

segments.name: Rest of World (Europe, LatAm)
segments.commentary: Revenue declined QoQ, linked to CPG one-off projects from these regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12% retained; management said confidence is reasonable and upside exists if pipeline converts.
Management expects a strong QoQ bounce-back in Q2 FY27, with CPG QoQ growth of 25%+ cited.
Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 20-21% for Q1 and FY27 held; 21-22% FY27 target not raised, with new Chief Technology and AI Officer and partnership functions offsetting FX benefit.
Further wage-hike impact of about 40-50 bps expected in Q2 FY27.
Long-term target of USD 200M revenue in FY28/FY29 reiterated as a stretch; organic growth needs to accelerate and inorganic deals are being pursued.
Transaction-related expenses end with Q1 FY27; no further such costs expected.
capex_capacity: M&A momentum described as strong, focused on data engineering and life sciences; one or two opportunities in advanced stage, including a letter of intent for a healthcare, life sciences and data engineering target.
New Chief Technology and AI Officer organization to combine AI products, agents, agent foundry, partnerships and service delivery excellence; not yet in the P&L.
Anthropic certification program underway with more than 200 staff enrolled; recognised partner of Anthropic and OpenAI.
Revenue mix: project-led 15-18%, managed services 65-70%, T&M the remainder.
Healtheon (RCM company, investee) is building agents for revenue cycle management.
demand_pricing: AI-led opportunities: about 15+ opportunities generated from AI prototypes; 14+ pursued, each worth about USD 0.5M in-year if won.
AI mix in Q1: about 80% of work has an AI element; about 35% is primary AI (AI solutions delivered directly to clients), versus 28% primary in FY26 and about half of work AI-impacted in FY26.
Productivity gains on completed projects range 30-80%, per management; clients are not yet passing these to tokens cost, as client typically supplies the AI tech stack.
Primary AI work currently less margin-accretive due to forward-deployed engineers and higher on-site mix; expected to become accretive over time with pricing and the agent foundry.
Wallet share: 2-5% at large enterprises with 20-30 partners; 100% at some clients where Latent View is the only partner. Little competition seen on new work or extensions at spending-centre level.
Six new accounts added in Q1 across financial services and auto components; new work for an AI data-centre infrastructure client.

qa_highlights.question: Does 12% FY27 guidance imply a steep QoQ ramp, and does it rely on closing pipeline deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 confirmed numbers give confidence; 12% needs pipeline extensions and new opportunities to come through, and it sees no downside beyond adverse events.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the 21% of revenue not in direct cost or SG&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining cost is payroll for sales and marketing and corporate management, in addition to SG&A (pure overhead) and direct cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will transaction-related expenses continue?
qa_highlights.answer: No; Q1 FY27 is the last quarter with transaction-related costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin reach 21-22% medium-term target soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to hold 20-21% for FY27, with investments in AI officer and partnership/CDO functions; no upgrade to margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much FX appreciation flows to margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investments will offset FX benefit; 21-22% guidance still in play but not raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much Databricks revenue was in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Net new Databricks revenue about USD 7.8M this quarter (vs about USD 7.5M last quarter), expected to rise to about USD 8.5M next quarter.

risks_watch: CPG recovery: management needs one-off projects replaced by extensions and new work; Q2 QoQ growth of 25%+ is promised but unproven.
Tech account insourcing and cost-reduction mandate at a large client: about USD 7-8M lost business; plug-gap timing uncertain.
Shift from managed services to fixed-fee, outcome-based models could add lumpiness and slower visibility.
AI productivity may reduce billable effort; token costs and client pushback on AI-led solutions flagged as emerging concerns.
Margin pressure: further 40-50 bps wage impact in Q2, new AI and partnership investments not yet in P&L.
Macro, geopolitical risks (including war) and dollar-rupee moves cited; new CEO setting out long-range plan with details expected in coming weeks.
key_quotes: So, overall, for the entire year as well, based on the opportunities that we currently see in the pipeline, we are still retaining our earlier guidance that we had given, in terms of 12% growth.
Rajan Venkatesan: Rohan, for this year, obviously, like I said, our guidance would still stay in the 21% to 22% range.
So, we are expecting that Q2 will be a bounce back in terms of the quarter-on-quarter trajectory.
Having joined only a few days ago, my immediate focus is very simple. I am listening, I'm learning, I'm engaging.
summary.management_tone: Management sounded confident on AI demand, pipeline and the 12% FY27 guidance, but was cautious on near-term numbers: the CEO said she had only joined days earlier and would share a long-range plan in coming weeks. Answers on the 12% growth, the 20-21% margin and the USD 200M target were hedged on pipeline conversion, and the 21-22% margin target was not raised.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12% was held, with management expecting a QoQ bounce-back in Q2 (CPG growth of 25%+ cited) and about USD 26M of pipeline, but Q1 USD revenue fell 3.5% QoQ, worse than guided, and no physical capacity additions were discussed.
